sourceHtml:
Shop

Monthly Grocery Baseline — Budget-Friendly High-Protein Core

The recurring baseline of primary, budget-friendly protein staples — not a variety list. Everything here is chosen for being cheap per gram of protein and easy to buy in bulk.

Where to buy:

  • Lidl / MyMarket — proteins, dairy, pantry, frozen items
  • Open-air market — vegetables and bananas (usually cheaper there)

A note on the prices below: these are ballpark estimates based on typical Greek discount-supermarket pricing, not scraped current prices — I couldn't pull reliable live prices for specific Lidl/MyMarket items. Treat this as a planning estimate to sanity-check against your first actual receipt, not an exact number.

Proteins (Animal)

Item Monthly Amount Est. Unit Price Est. Cost
Whole chicken 5-5.5 kg (raw, whole; ~3 average birds) ~€4.00/kg ~€21
Canned tuna (in water) 6-8 cans ~€1.75/can ~€12
Eggs (medium) 10 dozen (12 packs of 10) ~€2.50/pack of 10 ~€30

Whole chicken note: cheaper than buying cuts separately, but a whole bird only yields ~45-50% of its raw weight as boneless, skinless meat (bone/skin/fat make up the rest) — corrected up from an earlier, too-optimistic yield estimate so the actual usable meat still covers ~600g/week of recipe use.

Subtotal: ~€63

Proteins (Dairy)

Item Monthly Amount Est. Unit Price Est. Cost
Greek yogurt (0-2%) 4-5 kg total ~€4.00/kg ~€18
Cottage cheese 2-2.5 kg total ~€4.50/kg ~€10
Whey protein powder 1 kg tub ~€18/tub (budget brand) ~€18
Milk (optional, for shakes) 4-6L ~€1.15/L ~€6

Subtotal: ~€52 (or ~€46 if skipping milk)

Carb Staples

Item Monthly Amount Est. Unit Price Est. Cost
Oats 1.5-2 kg ~€1.75/kg ~€3
White rice 2-2.5 kg ~€1.75/kg ~€4
Potatoes (white) 2-2.5 kg ~€1.20/kg ~€3
Whole grain bread 2 loaves ~€2.00/loaf ~€4

Subtotal: ~€14

Fats

Item Monthly Amount Est. Unit Price Est. Cost
Olive oil 500ml-750ml ~€7.00/L ~€4-5
Peanut butter (or almond butter) 1 jar ~€3-4 (peanut) / ~€6-7 (almond) ~€3-7

Subtotal: ~€7-12

Vegetables & Bananas (open-air market, weekly)

Hardest to pin down since it's whatever's cheap that week, but as a rough weekly budget:

Item Est. Weekly Cost Est. Monthly Cost
Vegetables + bananas ~€10-15/week ~€40-60

Frozen (Lidl/MyMarket)

Item Monthly Amount Est. Unit Price Est. Cost
Frozen fruit ~1 kg ~€3.50/kg ~€3.5
Frozen vegetables (optional) ~1 kg if used ~€2/kg ~€2 (if used)

Estimated Total Monthly Cost

Category Est. Cost
Proteins (animal) ~€63
Proteins (dairy) ~€46-52
Carbs ~€14
Fats ~€7-12
Vegetables/bananas ~€40-60
Frozen fruit (+ optional veg) ~€3.5-5.5
Total ~€175-205/month

This is squarely a budget-focused number for a high-protein diet — the biggest swing factors are the whey protein (skip it and save ~€18 if you'd rather hit protein from food alone) and how much you end up spending at the open-air market week to week.

How to Use This

  • Buy proteins, dairy, and pantry items once a month or split into two trips — chicken keeps well frozen if bought in bulk
  • Buy vegetables and bananas weekly at the open-air market
  • Keep a bag of frozen fruit on hand as a fallback rather than relying only on fresh
  • This list is intentionally narrow — it's your core, not everything you'll ever eat. Add in whatever's cheap and available that week without needing to update this baseline
  • After your first real shopping trip, swap these estimated prices for your actual receipt totals — that'll make this budget section genuinely accurate instead of a rough guess
